The SAE occurred 110 days after the first dose of donanemab and 54 days after the third dose, which was the most recent dose. The reviewer did not identify a role for donanemab in the SAE because the onset of the event occurred close to five-times the half-life of donanemab, when exposure to donanemab would be low.
L3224: ## Acute Kidney Injury
L3225: One SAE of acute kidney injury was reported in one participant in Phase 2 and 3 Studies while on treatment with donanemab or within 57 days of treatment (I5T-MC-AACI-(b) (6)). The SAE occurred 51 days after the first dose of donanemab and 23 days after the second dose. The reviewer did not establish a role for donanemab in the SAE because the concurrent events of pneumothorax and multiple rib fractures, which were likely contributory.
L3226: ## Acute respiratory failure
L3227: One SAE of acute respiratory failure was reported on one donanemab-treated participant in Phase 2 and 3 Studies while on treatment or within 57 days of treatment (I5T-MC-AACT-(b) (6)). In this case, a role for donanemab could not be established in the SAE with fatal outcome because risk factors for acute respiratory failure existed in the case including multifocal pneumonia and a medical history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The reader is referred to the Deaths section of this review for further the narrative for this participant.

L3365: A higher frequency of donanemab-treated participants compared to placebo-treated had shift to low lymphocyte counts in Study AACG; however, the clinical significance of this is unknown, given the small magnitude of difference in mean values between donanemab and placebo arms. In Study AACG, a higher frequency of donanemab-treated participants compared to placebo-treated had shift from normal to low for lymphocyte with CTCAE Grade 1 toxicity (16.8% versus 9.6%, respectively).45 Mean change from baseline for lymphocyte showed statistically significant lower values in the donanemab arm compared to placebo (p values &lt; 0.05) at Weeks 12, 24, and 36; however, mean differences were small (no greater than 0.10 \times 10^9/L, normal reference range for lymphocytes of 0.8 - 3.0 \times 10^9/L). The maximal minimum value for lymphocyte count in Study AACG was 0.41 \times 10^9/L (occurring at Week 24). By Week 76, the mean difference in change from baseline between placebo and donanemab arms had decreased to 0.05 \times 10^9/L. In the all-donanemab pool, 10.1% of donanemab-treated subjects with normal baseline for lymphocytes had shift to CTCAE Grade 1 for decreased lymphocytes.46 The maximal minimum value for the all-donanemab pool for lymphocyte count among Week 12, 24, and 36 visits was 0.29 \times 10^9/L (occurring at Week 12).

L3374: ## Acute kidney injury
L3375: In Study AACG, the donanemab and placebo arms had the same frequency of participants reporting the TEAE of acute kidney injury (2%, 2/131 and 2/125, respectively).
L3376: In the all-donanemab pool, acute kidney injury was reported in 6 participants (6/1304, 0%). In five of the six participants, the acute kidney injury occurred within 57 days of treatment with donanemab. One of the five events was an SAE (I5T-MC-AACI-(b) (6)). In three of the five events, a role for donanemab in the events could not be established because of concurrent events that were likely contributory (pneumothorax and rib fractures/I5T-MC-AACI-(b) (6) severe small intestinal obstruction/I5T-MC-AACG-(b) (6) and Covid-19 infection/I5T-MC-AACI-(b) (6)). In the fourth event, a role could not be established as the lab was drawn prior to the first infusion of donanemab (I5T-MC-AACI-(b) (6)). In the remaining case, a role could not be established because of negative rechallenge (I5T-MC-AACI-(b) (6)). The event occurred 22 days after the 3rd dose and the patient went on to have three more doses without reoccurrence. None of the TEAEs of acute kidney injury led to treatment discontinuation or study withdrawal.

L3498: ## 8.5. Analysis of Submission-Specific Safety Issues
L3499: ## 8.5.1. ARIA
L3500: Monoclonal antibodies directed against aggregated forms of beta amyloid, can cause ARIA, characterized as ARIA with edema (ARIA-E), observed on MRI as brain edema or sulcal effusions, and ARIA with hemosiderin deposition (ARIA-H), which includes microhemorrhage and superficial siderosis. ARIA-H can occur spontaneously in patients with Alzheimer's disease. ARIA-H of any cause and ARIA-E can occur together, and ARIA-H associated with monoclonal antibodies directed against aggregated forms of beta amyloid generally occurs in association with an occurrence of ARIA-E. ARIA is usually asymptomatic, although serious and life-threatening events, including seizure and status epilepticus, rarely can occur. Rarely, fatal outcomes have been observed in clinical trials of monoclonal antibodies directed against aggregated forms of beta amyloid. When present, reported symptoms associated with ARIA include headache, confusion, visual changes, dizziness, nausea, and gait difficulty. Focal neurologic deficits may also occur. Symptoms associated with ARIA usually resolve over time. The following section focuses on findings of ARIA observed in donanemab clinical trials.
L3501: ## Summary
L3502: In blinded study AACI, three cases of ARIA had fatal outcome. No ARIA cases were reported to have fatal outcome in Study AACG or the all-donanemab pool. Serious ARIA-E cases were reported in 2% of donanemab-treated participants in Study AACG and 1% of participants in the all-donanemab-treated pool. ARIA occurred in 37% of donanemab-treated subjects compared to 8% of placebo in Study AACG. ARIA-E occurred in 27% in donanemab-treated participants compared to 1% of placebo in Study AACG. ARIA-H occurred in 30% in the donanemab arm compared to 7% on placebo in Study AACG. Symptomatic ARIA-E was reported in 3% of participants in the all-donanemab pool. No events of intracerebral hemorrhage &gt; 1 cm were
L3503: reported in Study AACG. Three events of intracerebral hemorrhage &gt; 1 cm were reported in the all-donanemab pool (0.2% [3/1304]).
L3504: Among donanemab-treated participants who experienced ARIA-E in Study AACG, 14% experienced symptoms. Symptoms reported in donanemab-treated participants with ARIA-E in Study AACG included headache and mental status changes. In the all-donanemab pool, 20% of donanemab-treated participants who experienced ARIA-E reported symptoms. The all-donanemab-treated pool showed similar findings compared to Study AACG of most frequent symptoms reported.
L3505: Among donanemab-treated participants in Study AACG, the maximum radiographic severity of ARIA-E was mild in 8%, moderate in 12%, and severe in 5% of participants. In the all-donanemab pool, 2% of participants had maximum radiographic severity of severe ARIA-E.
L3506: In participants who developed ARIA-E, approximately 95% experienced their first ARIA-E event by the 6th donanemab infusion in the all-donanemab pool. The first episode of ARIA-E had resolved by 20 weeks in 89% of donanemab-treated participants in Study AACG. Among donanemab-treated participants in Study AACG, 3% experienced more than one episode of ARIA-E.
L3507: In donanemab-treated participants in Study AACG, serious ARIA-E occurred at higher frequency in homozygous carriers for ApoE \epsilon4 compared to noncarriers (4% versus none, respectively). Donanemab-treated participants with concurrent antithrombotic use had similar frequencies of ARIA compared to participants without concurrent antithrombotic use in Study AACG. ARIA-E occurred with higher frequency in donanemab-treated participants &lt; 75 years of age compared to \ge75 years of age in Study AACG and the all-donanemab treated pool. Higher frequencies of ARIA-E and ARIA-H was observed in donanemab-treated participants with microhemorrhage present at baseline compared to participants without microhemorrhage present at baseline in Study AACG and the all-donanemab pool.
L3508: ## Methods
L3509: In the key safety studies, ARIA events were recorded as adverse events and as MRI findings. ARIA-E findings were required to be reported as adverse events by investigators, but this was not specified for ARIA-H events. This reviewer considered the dataset containing MRI findings to be the more comprehensive dataset for ARIA findings and as a result, analyses in this section use the MRI dataset unless otherwise specified.
L3510: The reader is referred to the appendix for further details on the recording of ARIA events, reporting of ARIA in the adverse events dataset and MRI dataset, dose modification for ARIA, and indications related to ARIA leading to permanent treatment discontinuation.

An MRI on Study Day 192 showed no change in findings compared to the previous MRI. In the second case, the non-serious seizure event had occurred 92 days after resolution of an ARIA-E event (partial seizures, I5T-MC-AACI-(b)(6)). L3601: In a January 13, 2023, response to an information request, the sponsor submitted data showing limited experience in continuing to administer donanemab in a patient with an ongoing episode of ARIA, and no experience in patients with ongoing severe ARIA.
L3602: ARIA-E or ARIA-H may occur in isolation or concurrently. ARIA-H occurring with ARIA-E has been noted in studies of other monoclonal antibodies. For example, in participants receiving bapineuzumab in two Phase 2 studies and one open-label extension study, incident ARIA-H occurred in 47% (17/36) of ARIA-E cases compared to 4% (7/177) of cases without ARIA-E. In the majority of cases, ARIA-H occurred on the same MRI or on an MRI scan immediately before or after the MRI with ARIA-E (14/17) and occurred in the same region as ARIA-E (8/14).63 In two Phase 3 studies of aducanumab, the incidence of brain microhemorrhages and localized superficial siderosis was increased in participants with ARIA-E compared with participants without ARIA-E. In participants without ARIA-E, the incidence of brain microhemorrhage and localized superficial siderosis was similar between the aducanumab and placebo groups.64
L3603: As noted by Sperling et al., ARIA-H occurring with ARIA-E suggests a shared pathophysiological mechanism and may be related to transient increases in vascular permeability. As postulated by Sperling et al, it is possible that depending on the location of the vessel, in the parenchyma

L3606: versus meninges, leakage of proteinaceous fluid could give lead to an increased signal on FLAIR images (ARIA-E) in the brain parenchyma (vasogenic edema) and leptomeningeal spaces (sulcal effusions), while leakage of red cells would result in ARIA-H, seen on T2*-weighted gradient echo MRI as cerebral microhemorrhages and hemosiderosis.63

L3656: ## 8.5.2. Hypersensitivity and Infusion Related Reactions
L3657: Serious cases of infusion related reaction were reported with 2% frequency in the donanemab arm compared to none on placebo in Study AACG. Serious cases of anaphylaxis were also reported in Phase 2 and 3 studies. A review of narratives of participants with infusion related reactions identified cases with increases and decreases in blood pressure and increases in heart rate at the time of infusion or within minutes following the end of the infusion. Infusion related reaction was among the most frequently reported TEAE in Study AACG, occurring in 8% of donanemab-treated subjects compared to none on placebo. Most TEAEs related to hypersensitivity and infusion-related reactions were mild or moderate in severity in Study AACG and the all-donanemab pool. Infusion related reaction was the most frequently reported TEAE leading to study withdrawal and treatment discontinuation, which was in part driven by protocol.

L3793: ## 8.9. Safety in the Postmarket Setting
L3794: ## 8.9.1. Safety Concerns Identified Through Postmarket Experience
L3795: Not applicable. Donanemab is a new molecular entity. It is not approved in other regions of the world.
L3796: ## 8.9.2. Expectations on Safety in the Postmarket Setting
L3797: The population of patients studied did not include patients with moderate or severe dementia, and safety outcomes in these patients is unknown.
L3798: The number of participants in the safety database with 12 months or more of exposure to donanemab is low. Monitoring of postmarketing adverse events will help provide additional information on the long-term safety of donanemab.
L3799: Conclusion about the carcinogenic potential of donanemab cannot be drawn, given the low
L3800: number of subjects with exposure to donanemab for at least 12 months or more.
L3801: A low number of subjects were enrolled in the placebo-controlled study of AACG within the demographic subgroups of age less than 65 years, age 85 years or older, non-White race, and Hispanic ethnicity, and conclusions regarding the impact of these demographic subgroups on the frequency of adverse events cannot be drawn.
L3802: Participants who experienced events of intracerebral hemorrhage &gt; 1 cm while on treatment with donanemab did not receive additional doses of donanemab after the events of intracerebral hemorrhage. The safety of continued treatment with donanemab in patients who have experienced intracerebral hemorrhage &gt; 1 cm while on donanemab therapy is unknown.
L3803: ## 8.9.3. Additional Safety Issues From Other Disciplines
L3804: Not applicable.
L3805: ## 8.10. Integrated Assessment of Safety
L3806: Safety findings from BLA 761248 are summarized below.
L3807: Relevant characteristics of the safety population. Participants with moderate or severe dementia were not included in the key clinical studies for safety. Treatment was discontinued in clinical studies once patients met criteria for amyloid plaque reduction. In Study AACG, a low number of subjects were enrolled with the following demographic characteristics: age less than 65 years, age 85 years or older, non-White race, and Hispanic ethnicity. Conclusions regarding the impact of these demographic characteristics on the frequency of adverse events cannot be drawn.
L3808: Adequacy of the safety database. The safety database does not fulfill minimum ICH guidance for exposure of at least 100 patients for 12 months at the proposed dose for drugs intended for long-term use. Therefore, the safety database is insufficient to adequately characterize the long-term safety of donanemab in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.
L3809: Deaths. There were four deaths occurring in participants who received donanemab. No deaths were attributable to donanemab. There was not an excess of deaths in the donanemab arm of Study AACG compared to placebo. At the time of the 90-Day Safety Update, 22 deaths were reported from the main study of AACI, which is still blinded, with an additional death reported from that blinded study after the 90-Day Safety Update. Three of the blinded cases reported ARIA with fatal outcome.
L3810: SAEs. SAEs were reported with equal frequency in donanemab and placebo arms in Study AACG. Pneumonia was the most frequent SAE reported in Study AACG in the donanemab arm. Pneumonia was reported in 4% of participants in the donanemab arm compared to 1% on placebo. ARIA-E, infusion related reaction, pulmonary embolism, and syncope were reported in
L3811: 2% of participants in the donanemab arm compared to none on placebo. In the all-donanemab pool, infection was the most frequently occurring SAE in the donanemab arm, occurring in 2% of participants.
L3812: **AEs Leading to Drug or Study Discontinuations.** Adverse events leading to study withdrawal were reported in 15% of donanemab-treated participants in Study AACG. The most frequent adverse events leading to study withdrawal in Study AACG were related to allergic reaction/hypersensitivity and ARIA-H microhemorrhage. Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were driven by protocol for ARIA events and infusion reactions. Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in approximately 31% of donanemab-treated subjects in Study AACG. The most frequent adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation in Study AACG were adverse events related to allergic reaction/hypersensitivity, ARIA-E, ARIA-H superficial siderosis, and ARIA-H microhemorrhages.
L3813: **Significant AEs.** Evaluation of severe AEs did not identify a new safety signal.
L3814: **Most Common AEs.** The most common TEAEs in Study AACG were ARIA-E, ARIA-H Microhemorrhage, and ARIA-H Superficial Siderosis. In Study AACG, treatment emergent AEs with at least 5% risk (rounded) and at least 2% greater than placebo in the donanemab arm were: ARIA-E (27% and 1% on donanemab and placebo, respectively), ARIA-H Microhemorrhage (20% and 5% on donanemab and placebo, respectively), ARIA-H Superficial Siderosis (17% and 2% on donanemab and placebo, respectively), nausea/vomiting (13% and 5% on donanemab and placebo, respectively), infusion related reaction (8% and none on donanemab and placebo, respectively), urinary tract infection (10% and 4% on donanemab and placebo, respectively), diarrhea (8% and 4% on donanemab and placebo, respectively), and anxiety (5% and 2% on donanemab and placebo, respectively). TEAEs occurring in less than 5% of donanemab-treated participants and at least 2% more than placebo in Study AACG included bronchitis/lower respiratory tract infection, hypotension, and bradycardia.
L3815: Vital sign, laboratory, and ECG evaluations in Study AACG showed higher frequencies of bradycardia and orthostatic changes in diastolic blood pressure and TEAEs related to bradycardia and hypotension in donanemab-treated participants compared to placebo.
L3816: **Pre-specified AE of interest:**
L3817: **Hepatic Safety** – There was no signal of hepatotoxicity identified.
L3818: **Immunogenicity** - In the all-donanemab pool, 84% participants who were evaluable for treatment emergent anti-drug antibody (ADA) responses had a positive postbaseline treatment emergent ADA status. All of these participants also had neutralizing antibody present.
L3819: **ARIA** – ARIA has been observed in other amyloid-directed monoclonal antibody therapies for the treatment of AD. In blinded study AACI, three cases of ARIA had fatal outcome. No ARIA cases were reported to have fatal outcome in Study AACG or the all-donanemab pool. Serious ARIA-E cases were reported in 1% of participants in the all-donanemab-treated pool.
L3820: Symptomatic ARIA-E was reported in 3% of participants in the all-donanemab pool.
L3821: Intracerebral hemorrhage &gt; 1 cm were reported in three subjects (0.2%) in the all-donanemab pool.
L3822: **Hypersensitivity and infusion-related reactions** – Serious cases of hypersensitivity and infusion
L3823: related reactions, including anaphylaxis, were observed in donanemab-treated participants. Serious infusion related reactions were reported in 2% of donanemab-treated participants compared to none on placebo in Study AACG. Increases and decreases in blood pressure and increases in heart rate were observed in participants with infusion related reactions. Suicidality - There was no evidence of an increased risk of suicidality with donanemab.

L3826: ## 10. Labeling Recommendations
L3827: ## 10.1. Prescription Drug Labeling
L3828: The applicant submitted proposed labeling on May 18, 2022, at the time of the third and final submission of a rolling submission.
L3829: ARIA is the primary observed safety issue associated with donanemab, as with lecanemab and aducanumab that are other members of this class of drugs. ARIA is characterized by radiographic findings on MRI and by symptoms associated with ARIA. Recommendations for clinical evaluation, including MRI monitoring and symptom recognition would be necessary should donanemab be approved in the future.
L3830: This reviewer recommends that in a future submission the prescribing information should include the observation of fatal cases of ARIA. This reviewer recommends the addition of class labeling language regarding the symptoms seen in some cases of ARIA and dose interruption recommendations.
L3831: This reviewer recommends that labeling include a Warnings and Precautions statements for ARIA and hypersensitivity and infusion related reactions. This reviewer recommends that increases and decreases in blood pressure and increases in heart rate observed in participants with infusion reactions be described in the Warnings and Precautions statement for hypersensitivity and infusion related reactions.
L3832: This reviewer recommends that the frequency of donanemab-treated participants with treatment emergent ADA responses and neutralizing antibodies be included in the immunogenicity section of labeling.
L3833: This reviewer recommends that the adverse reactions of hypotension and bradycardia be
L3834: included under the Adverse Reactions table in Section 6 of labeling as less common adverse reactions observed with donanemab treatment.

L3853: ## 13.2. Additional Narratives of Serious Cases of ARIA-E and ARIA-H
L3854: ARIA-E, ARIA-H (I5T-MC-AACG-[REDACTED](b) (6))
L3855: 78-year-old female with past medical history of mild cognitive impairment, dyslipidemia, depression, hypothyroidism, APOE genotype carrier \epsilon 4\epsilon 4 who developed the SAEs of ARIA-E and ARIA-H, 63 days after starting treatment with donanemab, and 5 days since the third dose of donanemab. Concomitant medications included escitalopram. The patient's screening MRI showed cortical superficial siderosis in the left frontal lobe. She received her first infusion of donanemab on Study Day 55. On Study Day 117, she experienced difficulty reading all except discrete words. On Study Day 120, she experienced word output difficulty. On Study Day 127, she was unable to recognize her home. On Study Day 128, the patient's MRI scan showed a new occurrence of moderate plus ARIA-E in right and left frontal, temporal-non-hippocampal, parietal, and occipital lobes with extent of 5 to 10 centimeters. The MRI scan also showed ARIA-H with 18 microhemorrhages in right and left frontal, parietal, and occipital (all 3 each), and 4 mm superficial siderosis in the left frontal lobe. These findings were reported as the SAEs of moderate ARIA-E and ARIA-H. On Study Day 113, the study drug was temporarily interrupted for the SAEs of ARIA-E and ARIA-H. On Study Day 130, she developed alexia without agraphia and Gerstmann syndrome. On Study Day 133, the patient's condition worsened. She had difficulty understanding instructions and was hospitalized for ARIA-E and ARIA-H on that day. She was treated with pulse steroid and intravenous methyl prednisolone from Study Day 134 through 136. On Study Day 136, she was able to write full sentences and was discharged from the hospital on a prednisone taper for 20 days. On Study Day 157, she had persistent symptoms of difficulty with word expression, comprehension, reading, writing and confusion. She was given an additional 14 days of prednisone. On Study Day 168, an MRI showed ARIA-E in right and left occipital region with mild FLAIR hyperintensity confined to sulcus and/or cortex/sub cortex white matter, affecting an area of less than 5 cm. Compared to the previous MRI, the ARIA-E had decreased in size and there was no change in the number of microhemorrhages. There was 10 mm superficial siderosis in the left frontal region. On Study Day 190, the patient's symptoms worsened (unspecified) and an MRI on Study Day 192 showed complete resolution of ARIA-E. The MRI also showed 29 microhemorrhages at right and left frontal (6 each), right and left parietal (3 each), right and left occipital (5 each), and left cerebellum (1); and unchanged superficial siderosis. The ARIA-E was reported as resolved that day. On Study Day 201, she had worsening confusion associated with alexia, agraphia, and acalculia. On Study Day 217, the patient was unstable on her feet. The SAE of ARIA-H and symptoms of dyslexia,
L3856: aphasia, visual agnosia, intellectual disability associated with ARIA-E were reported as not resolved at the time of the data cut-off on Study Day 234.
L3857: *Reviewer comment: A role for donanemab in the events of ARIA-E and ARIA-H is likely given the time between AE onset and dosing of donanemab, and because ARIA has been associated with aducanumab and lecanemab, approved amyloid-directed monoclonal antibody drugs.*
L3858: ARIA-E, pneumonia, (I5T-MC-AACG-[REDACTED](b) (6))
L3859: 78-year-old female with history of AD, anaphylactic reaction and drug hypersensitivity (allergies to sulfa, methotrexate, and vicodin), APOE genotype carrier \epsilon 4\epsilon 4, who was found to have ARIA-E of severe severity on MRI scan performed on Study Day 73, 16 days after the 3rd dose of donanemab. In addition, the MRI showed 6 new areas of cortical superficial siderosis of the CNS. On Study Day 75, a CT scan of the head showed white matter disease and cerebral edema. On Study Day 75, 18 days after the 3rd dose of donanemab, the patient experienced an adverse event of moderate hypersensitivity/infusion related reaction characterized by vomiting and the SAE of right lower lobe pneumonia (severe in intensity). She presented to the ER with increased confusion, weakness, and emesis. She received ondansetron, azithromycin, ceftriaxone, and levofloxacin. Also on that day, she had moderate hypoglycemia, moderate asthenia, and moderate decreased appetite. The hypoglycemia resolved on Study Day 76 and the vomiting resolved on Study Day 77.
L3860: On Study Day 87, the patient was noted to back to her baseline mental status. The AE of decreased appetite and the SAE of pneumonia resolved on Study Day 115. On Study Day 173, ARIA-E was noted as recovered/resolved. The AEs of superficial siderosis of the CNS and asthenia was not recovered/resolved at the time of study completion. The study drug was permanently discontinued due to the SAE of ARIA-E per protocol.
L3861: *Reviewer comment: A role for donanemab in the event of ARIA-E is likely given the time between AE onset and dosing of donanemab, and because ARIA has been associated with aducanumab and lecanemab, approved amyloid-directed monoclonal antibody drugs. A role for donanemab in the event of pneumonia cannot be ruled out given that the AE occurred within a time period when the patient was exposed to donanemab. Potentially contributory factors include the concurrent event of vomiting. Vomiting was identified as an infusion related reaction in the narrative; however, this appears unlikely given onset 15 days after the most recent infusion. Vomiting may be secondary to the SAE of ARIA-E as onset occurred within two days of onset of ARIA-E. The AE of superficial siderosis of the CNS is likely related to donanemab given that superficial siderosis of the CNS has been associated with aducanumab and lecanemab, approved amyloid-directed monoclonal antibody drugs.*

L3979: ## 13.5. Recording and Reporting of ARIA, and Dose Modification and Treatment Discontinuations Related to ARIA
L3980: ## Recording of ARIA Events
L3981: ARIA events were recorded as adverse events and as MRI findings. The submission includes two datasets containing ARIA events, one recorded as adverse events and one as MRI findings.
L3982: ARIA-E findings were required to be reported as adverse events by investigators, but this was not specified for ARIA-H events.72 Consistent with this, this reviewer noted a higher number of participants experiencing at least one ARIA-H event in the MRI dataset compared to the adverse event dataset (differences greater than 50 participants).
L3983: 72 Noted in a response dated September 2, 2022, to an information request dated September 1, 2022.
L3984: The sponsor considered the MRI data to be the more comprehensive and definitive source for identification of ARIA-H rather than the adverse event dataset.73
L3985: Small differences in the number of participants experiencing at least one ARIA-E event were noted in the adverse event and MRI datasets (difference &lt; 5 participants). The sponsor noted that these differences were due in part to differences in timing of data entry in the two datasets relative to the data cutoff points.74
L3986: *Reviewer comment: This reviewer considered the dataset containing MRI findings to be the more comprehensive dataset for ARIA findings and as a result, analyses in this section used the MRI dataset unless otherwise specified.*
L3987: Denominators for analyses in this section are the safety population (those who received at least one dose of study drug).
L3988: ## Reporting of ARIA in the Adverse Events Dataset
L3989: The sponsor notes that the protocols did not specify terminology for investigators to use if ARIA-H occurred; therefore, events of ARIA-H were recorded under multiple preferred terms.75
L3990: For analyses of adverse events related to ARIA-H, the following preferred terms were used:
L3991: - Amyloid-related imaging abnormality-microhemorrhage and hemosiderin deposits
- Brain stem microhemorrhage
- Cerebellar microhemorrhage
- Cerebral hemosiderin deposit
- Cerebral microhemorrhage
- Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system
L3992: *Reviewer comment: The sponsor proposed to include intracerebral hemorrhage as one of the terms contributing to ARIA-H; however, similar to events reported in the prescribing information for aducanumab and lecanemab, events related to intracerebral hemorrhage were evaluated separately from ARIA-H.76*

L4000: In the event of finding ARIA-E on MRI, the investigator was to complete the case report form regarding the presence or absence of symptoms related to the ARIA-E.
L4001: Symptoms related to symptomatic ARIA-E events were captured in a dedicated case report form; however, seriousness of the symptoms was not collected.79 If the event met ICH criteria for an SAE, the event was reported as an SAE. Studies AACG, AACH, and AACI did not have dedicated case report forms to collect ARIA-H symptoms.80 Symptomatic ARIA-H was a notable event when serious or listed as a reason for discontinuation.
L4002: Similar to other AEs, ARIA events reported as adverse events were categorized as mild, moderate, and severe by the investigator based on severity assessment guidelines.
L4003: ## Recording and Reporting of ARIA in the MRI Dataset
L4004: In Study AACG, per study protocol, MRIs were performed at screening (within 9 weeks of Study Day 1), Weeks 4 (Visit 3, prior to the 2nd infusion), 12 (Visit 5, prior to the 4th infusion), 16 (Visit 6, prior to the 5th infusion), 24 (Visit 8, prior to the 7th infusion), 36 (Visit 11, prior to the 10th infusion), 52 (Visit 15, prior to the 14th infusion), 76, and the Early Discontinuation visit. Additionally, the protocol indicated that an unscheduled MRI be performed if a participant developed more than one symptom suggestive of ARIA-E or a single symptom suggestive of ARIA-E of sufficient severity. If ARIA was present, then repeat MRIs every 4 to 6 weeks until resolution of ARIA-E or stabilization of ARIA-H was recommended. MRIs were read locally, and then sent to a centralized MRI vendor for analysis. The MRI at Week 12 (Visit 5) was to be performed and reviewed 2 weeks prior to the 4th donanemab infusion (Visit 5).

L4023: ## **ARIA-E Severity Rating Scale**
L4024: **No/Questionable ARIA-E:** *Normal to subtle sulcal or cortical FLAIR hyperintensity, most likely artifactual.*
L4025: **Mild ARIA-E:** *Mild FLAIR hyperintensity confined to sulcus and/or cortex/subcortex white matter (with or without gyral swelling and sulcal effacement), which affects an area of less than 5 cm in a single greatest dimension. Only a single region of involvement detected.*
L4026: **Moderate ARIA-E:** *Moderate involvement (area of FLAIR hyperintensity measuring 5-10 cm in single greatest dimension), or more than one site of involvement, each measuring less than 10 cm in a single greatest dimension.*
L4027: **Severe ARIA-E:** *Severe involvement (area of FLAIR hyperintensity measuring greater than 10 cm in single greatest dimension white matter) and /or sulcal involvement (with associated gyral swelling and sulcal effacement). One or more separate/independent sites of involvement may be noted.*
L4028: **Non-evaluable:** *Select when image quality is not sufficient to determine the presence or absence of ARIA-E (incorrect MRI parameters, motion degradation, missing FLAIR, etc.). Please provide reasons for why the images are not evaluable in the comments of Section 5.*
L4029: The figure was copied from the Brain MRI Worksheet Completion Guidelines noted in the sponsor's response dated September 2, 2022, to an information request dated September 1, 2022.
L4030: Similar ARIA-E severity rating scales were used for Study AACH, AACI, and AACN, except that moderate ARIA-E was further subdivided into the categories of mild+, moderate, and moderate+. 81
L4031: Mild, moderate, and severe categories were not used to grade ARIA-H radiographically. 82 Instead, ARIA-H radiographic findings were recorded based on shifts from baseline, and the following categories were used:
L4032: - no change from baseline
- microhemorrhage increase from baseline \le 4
- microhemorrhage increase from baseline &gt; 4
- microhemorrhage increase nonevaluable
- treatment-emergent superficial siderosis
- treatment-emergent macrohemorrhage (intracerebral hemorrhage)

L4047: If dose reduction was required, the donanemab dose was reduced to the next lower dose (700 mg for a 1400 mg dose or placebo for a 700 mg dose). All cases of ARIA-E required further unscheduled MRI scans every 4-6 weeks until ARIA-E has resolved. If the study drug was restarted, patients were given donanemab 700 mg or placebo, depending on the original study arm to which the patient was randomized. An unscheduled safety MRI was required 4-6 weeks after dose restarts. If ARIA-E symptoms and radiologic findings were not completely resolved within 16 weeks, the patient was permanently discontinued from donanemab treatment.
L4048: In Study AACG, no dose reductions were done for ARIA-H. Patient were discontinued from dosing if they developed any increase in ARIA-H accompanied by clinically significant symptoms; had &gt;4 new microhemorrhages, &gt; 1 new area of superficial siderosis or significant worsening of pre-existing superficial siderosis; or any intracerebral hemorrhage, regardless of symptoms. All new cases of ARIA-H required unscheduled MRI scans every 4-6 weeks until ARIA-H has stabilized without new findings.
L4049: In contrast to Study AACG, Studies AACH Part B, AACI Safety Addendum, and AACN-Dona cohort did not include dose reduction for the development of ARIA. In these three studies, for participants who developed ARIA during the titration period, the study drug could be temporarily suspended, continue at 700 mg dose temporarily or throughout the remainder of the treatment period, or increased to 1400 mg dose if the participant had received three doses of 700 mg.
L4050: Studies AACH Part B, AACI Safety Addendum, and AACN-Dona Cohort had more permissive dosing in ARIA-H management compared to Study AACG. The following figure shows guidance for management of ARIA-H in Study AACH Part B from the Manual of Operations.

L4059: ## Indications Related to ARIA Leading to Permanent Treatment Discontinuation by Protocol
L4060: Per Study AACG protocol, treatment with donanemab was permanently discontinued in patients for the following conditions related to ARIA:
L4061: - Second incidence of ARIA-E that occurred after a previous dose reduction or temporary discontinuation of donanemab
- Any increase in ARIA-H accompanied by clinically significant symptoms
- &gt;4 new microhemorrhages, &gt; 1 new area of superficial siderosis or significant worsening of pre-existing superficial siderosis, or any intracerebral hemorrhage, regardless of symptoms
- An ARIA-E event reported as an SAE
L4062: The protocols for Studies AACH Part B, AAC1 Safety Addendum and AACN Dona-Cohort differed from the protocol for Study AACG for indications leading to permanent discontinuation for ARIA-related conditions and included the following conditions:
L4063: - No observable resolution of moderate +/-severe ARIA-E
- No observable resolution of symptomatic ARIA-E or resolutions of symptoms of ARIA-E
- Symptoms of ARIA-E or ARIA-H are clearly related to a serious adverse event
- No observable resolution of symptoms of ARIA-H
- Intracerebral hemorrhage

L4124: Assessment of Intensity
The investigator will make an assessment of intensity for each AE and SAE reported during the study and assign it to one of the following categories:
Mild: An event that is easily tolerated by the participant, causing minimal discomfort, and not interfering with everyday activities.
Moderate: An event that causes sufficient discomfort and interferes with normal everyday activities.
Severe: An event that prevents normal everyday activities. An AE that is assessed as severe should not be confused with an SAE. Severe is a category utilized for rating the intensity of an event, and both AEs and SAEs can be assessed as severe.
L4125: Scatter plot showing Peak On-Treatment Bilirubin (xULN) on the Y-axis (log scale, 0.01 to 100) versus Peak On-Treatment ALT or AST (xULN) on the X-axis (log scale, 0.1 to 100). The plot is divided into four quadrants by dashed lines at Y=2 and X=3. The top right quadrant is labeled 'Potential Hy's Law'. The bottom right quadrant is labeled 'Temple's Corollary'. The data points are clustered primarily in the bottom left quadrant (low ALT/AST, low Bilirubin).
L4126: Product-Limit Failure Curves
With Number of Subjects at Risk and 95% Hall-Wellner Bands
This figure displays the Product-Limit Failure Curves (Kaplan-Meier curves) showing the probability of the first ARIA-E event over time (Days from First Treatment) for three treatment groups: Heterozygote, Homozygote, and Non-Carrier. L4132: Figure 5 displays four line graphs showing the Adjusted mean change from baseline (\pm SE) over time (Weeks 0, 12, 24, 36, 52, 64, 76) for Placebo (gray line) and Donanemab (purple line) treatment arms. The sample sizes (n) are listed below the X-axis for each time point.
The four endpoints measured are CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog 13, ADCS-iADL, and MMSE.
CDR-SB (Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes): The adjusted mean change from baseline increases over time for both groups. The Donanemab group shows a significantly greater increase than the Placebo group at Week 52 (p < 0.01), Week 64 (p < 0.01), and Week 76 (p < 0.05).
ADAS-Cog 13 (Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale): The adjusted mean change from baseline increases over time for both groups. The Donanemab group shows a significantly greater increase than the Placebo group at Week 76 (p < 0.05).
ADCS-iADL (Activities of Daily Living): The adjusted mean change from baseline decreases over time for both groups. The Donanemab group shows a significantly greater decrease than the Placebo group at Week 36 (p < 0.05), Week 52 (p < 0.01), Week 64 (p < 0.05), and Week 76 (p < 0.01).
MMSE (Mini-Mental State Examination): The adjusted mean change from baseline decreases over time for both groups. The Donanemab group shows a significantly greater decrease than the Placebo group at Week 64 (p < 0.05) and Week 76 (p < 0.01).
